newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded sharply higher early in the week on light to moderate demand and light offerings, USDA said. However, at the end of the week, prices did stabilize as demand became very light.
Retail demand was for immediate needs, while some forward interest was noted on closely trimmed chuck cuts.

Rib and loin cuts traded higher as processors entered the week in their best sold position in quite some time, after last week's large volume of trading. Chuck and round cuts also traded higher, but chuck cuts ended with weak undertone, as inventories on these cuts were rather uneven.

Closely trimmed items encountered better demand, compared to their commodity counterparts, as these cuts were seen as better values. Beef trimmings traded higher on moderate demand and light offerings. Increased raw material cost helped stimulate the fed cattle and blended coarse ground items sharply higher on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings. Fed cattle grinds experienced the biggest advances.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 5.00 to 7.00 higher Select and Choice chuck primal 4.00 to 5.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 4.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 5.50 to 6.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 4.50 to 5.00 higher; Beef trimmings 4.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 4.00 to 10.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 4.64 at 107.15; 700/850 Up 4.81 at 106.59; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 4.61 at 102.32; 700/850 Up 4.71 at 101.84.
COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW

CUTOUT The market for lean processing beef moved higher early in the week on anticipation of short offerings as cow numbers lessened at auction. However, demand from grinders failed to develop as the week progressed and further price advances were halted as sellers lowered asking prices to move product. Good demand for 65% and 85% beef trimmings saw brisk business at higher prices early in the week but tapered off later.

Demand remained good for 100% lean items again this week and price levels continued on their upward track. Utility carcasses steady to 1.00 higher; Cutter not established; 90% boneless beef mostly 2.00-3.00 higher; 85% 3.50 higher; 75% .50-1.50 higher; 65% mostly 3.00 higher. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, April 10, 1997 was estimated at 83.87 per cwt., up 2.09 from a week ago Friday.
